messages:
marta: Heads-up — since ~08:13 UTC we're seeing repeated 502s from the provisioner when creating GPU nodes for tenant-42 in us-west1. Autoscaler shows ``throttled=true`` and pool capacity isn't increasing. Kibana traces show missing trace_id between provisioner and scheduler services.

jon: got it. can you paste the kibana query you used?

marta: sure — KQL to look at the failed provisioner requests:
```
service:provisioner AND env:prod AND http.status_code:502 AND kubernetes.namespace:tenant-42 AND @timestamp >= now-1h
```
results show a burst starting 08:12:10 UTC.

alertbot: :warning: Alert firing: GPUPoolHighProvisionLatency (us-west1-pool-4) — 5m avg > 45s (firing since 08:15 UTC)

lee: can we correlate with prometheus? maybe autoscaler hit API rate limits or cloud quota.

jon: quick prom query to check API errors and autoscaler throttles:
```
sum(rate(k8s_api_requests_total{verb=\"create\",resource=\"nodes\",code=~\"5..\",region=\"us-west1\"}[5m])) by (code)
(sum(rate(k8s_controller_manager_queue_duration_seconds_count{controller=\"cluster-autoscaler\"}[5m])) > 0)
```
this'll show 5xx create node spikes and queue backlog.

marta: prom shows `k8s_api_requests_total{code=\"503\"}` spike matching 08:12. autoscaler logs show `throttled: true` and errors `429` from cloud provider.

anika: 429 from cloud provider suggests we've hit quota or transient rate limiting. do we have per-tenant egress / NAT ephemeral exhaustion in us-west1? that could make control-plane calls fail intermittently.

lee: checked NAT gw logs — many short-lived connections from provisioner pods to cloud API at the same time, ephemeral port reuse look suspicious. NAT conntrack skew could cause failed multiplexing.

marta: here's a snippet from the provisioner pod logs around 08:12 (truncated):
```
2026-02-11T08:12:11Z provisioner-42 ERROR failed to create node: cloudapi: request failed status=503 body=\"service unavailable\"
2026-02-11T08:12:12Z provisioner-42 WARN retrying attempt=3 backoff=2.1s
2026-02-11T08:12:13Z provisioner-42 ERROR missing trace_id on outgoing call to scheduler, trace header not propagated
```

jon: missing trace_id is interesting — if provisioner isn't propagating traces, Kibana can't stitch. could be a side-effect of the 503 error path stripping headers. let's search in loki for trace propagation errors:
```
{app=\"provisioner\", level=~\"ERROR|WARN\"} |= \"missing trace_id\" | json | line_format \"${message} ${trace_id}\"
```

marta: loki returns ~120 occurrences during the burst, same pod set.

anika: two parallel problems then: 1) cloud provider rate limit / NAT exhaustion causing 5xx/429; 2) error-handling code path drops trace headers, making correlation hard. both increase SLO noise.

lee: short-term mitigation ideas:
- scale provisioner replicas to spread NAT usage (:point_up: be careful with API calls though)
- add exponential jitter and increase backoff base to reduce storming
- pin ephemeral NAT allocation per-node (cloud dependent)
- add trace header propagation in error path

jon: also propose adding a tenant label to the problematic alerts so tenant-caused noisy provisioning doesn't spam global SLO channel. e.g. only page when cluster-wide failure, not single-tenant transient.

marta: landing action: I'll patch provisioner to preserve trace headers in the 503/429 retry branch and raise backoff to 5s base. I'll open infra ticket to investigate NAT port limits and request a quota bump with cloud.

anika: for observability follow-ups:
- modify GPUPoolHighProvisionLatency alert to include `tenant != tenant-42` for paging for now, and add a quieter `notice` alert for tenant-scoped failures.
- add a grafana panel that correlates `k8s_api_requests_total{region=\"us-west1\"}` with `provisioner_errors_total` and NAT ephemeral usage — helps runbook triage.

jon: can someone run a quick restart of the provisioner deployment in us-west1 so new image with trace fix can be deployed when ready? and remove noisy pages from the incident channel for now.

marta: I've bumped replica count to 4 to spread requests, rolled a small backoff config change (non-code) — we see reduced 503s already. filing follow-up tickets: INFRA-3253 (NAT port analysis) and SRE-4121 (alert tuning + dashboard).

lee: noted. I'll triage NAT logs and reach out to cloud support.

anika: thanks all — good triage. please add the Kibana/Loki query snippets to the incident doc so support can reproduce. tagging @oncall for visibility :eyes:

alertbot: Incident updated — INFRA-3253 created by marta.

marta: final: will follow up with a PR for the trace propagation fix and a runbook for tenant-scoped provisioning storms. closing this thread for now, will reopen if stats worsen. :white_check_mark:
